_comment: The defect being guarded against was itself a check that covered nothing: ensure_local_dirs()
called mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) and nothing else, which is a no-op on a directory
that already exists -- and storage/uploads, storage/clips, storage/temp and
storage/transcripts are committed as .gitkeep files, so they exist in every clone. The app
therefore booted onto a bind mount it could not write to, and the failure surfaced hundreds of
lines away as sqlite3.OperationalError: attempt to write a readonly database.
So a mutation run matters more here than usual: the thing that broke was a guard, and a guard
that cannot fail is exactly what the first mutation below restores. If it escapes, this fix has
the same shape as the bug it replaces.
The command runs the two modules that own this behaviour together, because the fix spans
config.py and both SQLite stores and a mutation in one can be caught by the other's tests.

mutations.name: no_write_probe_at_all
mutations.why: restores the original defect exactly: existence accepted as writability, so the app boots onto an unwritable mount

mutations.name: probe_asks_about_mode_bits_instead_of_writing
mutations.old:
probe = directory / f".write-probe-{os.getpid()}"
    try:
        # "xb" so an unexpected leftover is an error rather than something we silently overwrite.
        with probe.open("xb") as handle:
            handle.write(b"")
mutations.why: swaps the real write for a mode-bit query, which is the wrong instrument: os.access reports what the bits say, and every case that bites (read-only bind mount, container UID no ACL covers) can present bits that look fine. Note an earlier version of this mutation ADDED the os.access check while leaving the write in place, and escaped -- correctly, since that is stricter rather than weaker and reintroduces nothing. The defect is replacing the write, not preceding it.

mutations.name: required_directory_failure_is_only_a_warning
mutations.why: an unwritable storage/ must be fatal at boot; downgrading it to a warning reproduces the reported crash, just with a log line nobody reads

mutations.name: optional_directory_failure_becomes_fatal
mutations.why: the opposite over-reach: assets/ is legitimately read-only, and refusing to boot over an unused emoji style would break a supported deployment

mutations.name: probe_leaves_its_file_behind
mutations.why: litter in uploads/ is not cosmetic -- that directory is enumerated by the API and the watch folder

mutations.name: history_store_stops_explaining_the_failure
mutations.why: this is the frame the report came from; without the translation the user gets SQLite's wording, which names neither the file nor the directory

mutations.name: job_store_stops_explaining_the_failure
mutations.why: both stores carry the pattern and only one was reported last time; the jobs database is simply reached later

mutations.name: unwritable_file_and_unwritable_directory_are_conflated
mutations.old:
elif path.exists() and not os.access(path, os.W_OK):
        cause = f"the file exists but is not writable by this user (uid {os.getuid()})"
mutations.new:
elif False:
        cause = f"the file exists but is not writable by this user (uid {os.getuid()})"
mutations.why: the two states call for different remedies, so collapsing them sends the reader to the wrong one

mutations.name: the_message_drops_sqlite_s_own_words
mutations.old: f"(SQLite said: {exc}). In Docker this is the storage bind mount: the image runs as "
mutations.new: f". In Docker this is the storage bind mount: the image runs as "
mutations.why: rewording must not discard the original text, which is what anyone will paste into a search engine

mutations.name: the_remedy_is_dropped_from_the_boot_failure
mutations.old: "`sudo chown -R 10001:10001 storage`, or switch the mount to a named volume "
mutations.new: "nothing you can do, or switch the mount to a named volume "
mutations.why: the reason the original was misdiagnosed is that the error said what failed and not what to do; the remedy is load-bearing
